dim_resolution.notes: it.id used only as join key with mi.info_type_id; since it.id is identity over 113 rows and mi.info_type_id values are guaranteed to reference existing it rows, the it join is a no-op and can be elided.

join_order.notes: Driver scan over title; for each surviving t_id, range-probe mc using mc_off[t_id..t_id+1].

join_order.build: mc_filtered (company_type_id==target_ct_id AND note contains '(VHS)' AND '(USA)' AND '(1994)')
join_order.notes: Three-substring note filter is highly selective; only proceed to mi probe if at least one mc row survives for this t_id.
Existence check; first matching mi row in range short-circuits the t_id qualification.

filters.predicate: note length >= 17 AND memmem(note,'(VHS)') AND memmem(note,'(USA)') AND memmem(note,'(1994)')
filters.notes: Order substring checks cheapest/most-selective first: '(VHS)' (rarest), then '(1994)', then '(USA)'. Length prefilter cuts NULL/short notes.

data_structures.mc_note_filter: varlen .off + .dat with memmem; three required needles

parallelism.notes: Each thread maintains local MIN string; final reduction picks lexicographically smallest. 12 cores → ~25 morsels.

memory_estimate.mc_columns_streamed: company_type_id + note.off+.dat accessed by row range

short_circuit_notes: For each t_id: iterate mc range; on first mc row passing ct_id + 3-substring note filter, set mc_ok and break.
If mc_ok: iterate mi range; on first mi row with info IN set, set mi_ok and break.
If both ok: fetch t.title (varlen), update thread-local MIN.
